evals.prompt: Review this typography. A dashboard body paragraph (role: body) is styled with `font-family: Inter; font-size: 16px; font-weight: 400;`. Inter is being used on a body role. Is the font family correct?
evals.expected_output: J1 FAILs: Plus Jakarta Sans is required for every role except the stylized label set (capitalized / small / tiny, which use Inter) — using Inter on a body role is a family mismatch. Fix: set font-family to Plus Jakarta Sans for the body role. Overall: NEEDS FIX.
evals.label: bad-example
evals.notes: Targets J1 — font family matches the role.
assertions: Identifies Inter used on a body role as wrong

evals.prompt: Review this typography. A section heading (role: heading2) is styled with `font-family: Plus Jakarta Sans; font-size: 32px; font-weight: 500;`. Weight 500 is used on a content heading. Is the weight correct?
evals.expected_output: J2 FAILs: headings and body use only 400 or 600; 500 is not permitted on a role-based content heading (700 is allowed only on Display and on shared-component chrome per component-standard) — 500 here is a weight violation. Fix: set the heading2 weight to 600 (or 400) per its typography.json value. Overall: NEEDS FIX.
evals.label: bad-example
evals.notes: Targets J2 — weight is 400 or 600, exceptions only.
assertions: Flags weight 500 on a content heading as not permitted

evals.prompt: Review this typography. A dashboard page title (role: heading1) is styled with `font-family: Plus Jakarta Sans; font-size: 28px; font-weight: 600;`. The size 28px was eyeballed. Is the size correct?
evals.expected_output: J3 FAILs: sizes must come from the fixed scale only (64 / 56 / 48 / 40 / 32 / 24 / 20 / 18 / 16 / 14 / 12 / 10) and 28px is an in-between value — the classic symptom of eyeballing instead of snapping to a role. Fix: a dashboard page title is heading1 → 48px (or, if intentionally smaller, snap to the nearest role — 40 / 32 / 24 — never an in-between value). Overall: NEEDS FIX.
evals.label: bad-example
evals.notes: Targets J3 — size snaps to the scale.
assertions: Identifies 28px as an off-scale in-between value
Recommends snapping to a scale value such as 48px

evals.notes: Targets J4 — line-height is a unitless ratio matching the role.
assertions: Recommends the unitless ratio 1.2 for H1/H2

evals.prompt: Review this typography. An all-caps eyebrow label uses role `capitalized` styled with `font-family: Inter; font-size: 12px; letter-spacing: 2px;` but the element has no `text-transform: uppercase` and the source text is lowercase. Is the role applied correctly?

evals.label: bad-example

assertions: Identifies the missing text-transform: uppercase on the capitalized role

evals.prompt: Review this typography. The text under review is the hero headline of the ahaslides.com marketing landing page, styled with `font-family: Plus Jakarta Sans; font-size: 56px; font-weight: 300; optical-sizing: auto;` — a brand/marketing asset being forced onto the product-UI scale. evals.expected_output: J7 FAILs: this scale governs in-app product UI (presenter, audience, editor, dashboard); a marketing/brand surface like a landing-page hero must NOT be forced onto this scale (note the weight 300 and optical sizing, which belong to the brand range 200-800). Fix: redirect this to aha-branding-typography, which owns marketing/brand type. Overall: NEEDS FIX.
evals.label: bad-example
evals.notes: Targets J7 — in scope: product UI, not marketing/brand.
assertions: Identifies the text as a marketing/brand landing-page asset out of scope
